exposure: antepartum management (including adjusted-dose low-molecular-weight heparin and monitoring by anti-Xa level, AT activity, and D-dimer)
outcome: pregnancy outcomes (live births, second-trimester abortions, early pregnancy losses)
cohort: The study included 17 pregnancies in 6 women with inherited AT deficiency treated at a single center between 2013 and 2024.
finding: Inherited antithrombin (AT) deficiency is an important factor contributing to adverse pregnancy outcomes, with a positive correlation observed between adequate anticoagulation (based on tight monitoring and timely LMWH adjustment) and improved pregnancy outcomes, despite a high prevalence of heparin resistance.
